existing_dag_preservation.rule: No Rust implementation PR may start before MAP-PR-011 is merged and has a passing fresh-context receipt.

execution_policy.risk_unit: one externally observable invariant cluster per PR
execution_policy.large_benchmarks: local evidence allowed; required CI must stay practical for one developer

pull_requests.title: Rust Engine Workspace, CI, and Frozen Oracle Baseline

objective.statement: Create a pure-Rust engine workspace and required Rust CI without moving simulation semantics yet.
objective.observable_success: `metroflow-core` and `metroflow-python` build; Rust tests are required; frozen Python oracle scenarios, schemas and performance baseline are committed before porting.

forbidden_changes: Do not change simulation outputs, backend defaults, scientific tolerances, map generator behavior or Python oracle semantics.
Do not delete or rename the existing `_metroflow_rust` API.

ordered_steps.action: Add RED tests requiring the two-crate layering and a Rust-required CI surface.
Split the workspace so `metroflow-core` has no PyO3/Python dependency and `metroflow-python` depends on core.
Keep `crates/metroflow-rust` as a compatibility facade.
Freeze representative Python oracle scenarios, public artifact schemas, runtime wall/RSS measurements and exact commands.
Add cargo fmt, clippy and cargo test to required CI; build the extension in parity jobs.

claim.allowed: the Rust migration workspace and frozen Python oracle baseline exist
claim.not_allowed: Rust is faster, complete, or default

stop_conditions: Existing MAP-PR-011 is not merged with a passing independent receipt.
The workspace split changes Python-visible behavior.
Required CI cannot build the Rust extension reproducibly.

pull_requests.title: Canonical Rust State, Units, IDs, RNG, and Checkpoint Schema

objective.statement: Define the complete canonical engine state contract in pure Rust before moving domain algorithms.
objective.observable_success: Every static/dynamic field has a typed Rust representation, unit, dtype, bounds, stable ID/index rule, RNG stream and versioned checkpoint encoding.

forbidden_changes: Do not move tick algorithms yet.
Do not collapse stable IDs into dense indices without a reversible map.
Do not change field precision merely to simplify Rust.

ordered_steps.action: Inventory every field reachable from SimulationState and publish a field contract.
Implement stable ID newtypes, checked index conversion, units and field-specific f32/f64 policy.
Implement named deterministic RNG streams and a versioned checkpoint envelope.
Implement Python-to-Rust import and Rust-to-Python diagnostic export for state only.
Add empty, maximum-bound, overflow, malformed-offset and round-trip fixtures.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_engine_state_contract.py -k 'overflow or malformed or unknown_version'

claim.allowed: the Rust state/checkpoint schema is complete and round-trippable
claim.not_allowed: the Rust engine implements simulation behavior

stop_conditions: A Python state field lacks a Rust owner or unit.
An ID/index conversion can overflow silently.
Checkpoint round-trip cannot preserve RNG and schema identity.

pull_requests.title: Static City, Network, DCEL, and Static Authority Port

objective.statement: Move all accepted static city-generation and graph-authority semantics into metroflow-core.
objective.observable_success: For the frozen matrix, Rust reproduces exact-mm topology, IDs, layers, turns, DCEL faces, zoning/static authority and fingerprints or emits an explicit versioned migration.

forbidden_changes: Do not re-tune morphology or alter MAP evidence.
Do not approximate exact-mm geometry with floating coordinates.
Do not weaken crossing, touch, DCEL or layer-transition tests.

ordered_steps.action: Port canonical records and exact geometry predicates first.
Port style generation and infrastructure budgets without changing public semantics.
Port graph compilation, turn legality, DCEL, block/static authority and fingerprints.
Compare every field and fingerprint against Python on frozen seeds/scales/styles.
Keep Python builders as oracle wrappers until final promotion.

targeted: cargo test -p metroflow-core city graph dcel
negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_static_city_parity.py -k 'crossing or touch or layer or overflow'

claim.allowed: Rust reproduces the accepted static-city authority on the frozen parity matrix
claim.not_allowed: Rust-generated maps are empirically realistic or traffic-valid

stop_conditions: Exact geometry or DCEL parity requires tolerance weakening.
A public fingerprint changes without a versioned migration.
The port modifies frozen MAP evidence.

pull_requests.title: Demand, Schedules, Controls, Events, and Multirate Scheduler Port

objective.statement: Move deterministic temporal orchestration inputs and demand lifecycle into Rust.
objective.observable_success: Rust reproduces population/schedule/trip activation, controls, event ordering and multirate cadence across pause, injection, clear and boundary cases.

forbidden_changes: Do not alter demand distributions, event precedence, tick numbering or random streams.
Do not make Python callbacks part of every tick.

ordered_steps.action: Port population and schedule records with stable ordering.
Port trip generation/activation and named RNG consumption.
Port control/event queue and exact ordering for inject, activate, clear and pause.
Port multirate scheduler and cadence metadata.
Run long boundary fixtures around tick zero, interval edges and simultaneous events.

targeted: cargo test -p metroflow-core demand scheduler events
negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_demand_scheduler_parity.py -k 'simultaneous or pause or boundary or malformed'

claim.allowed: Rust reproduces the declared temporal and demand contract
claim.not_allowed: Rust changes demand realism or validates external demand

stop_conditions: RNG consumption cannot be matched or explicitly versioned.
Simultaneous event order is ambiguous.
A required per-tick Python callback remains.

pull_requests.title: Rust-Owned Routing, Candidate Cache, and Reroute Engine

objective.statement: Move the complete legal routing state and cache lifecycle into metroflow-core.
objective.observable_success: Dynamic potentials, ranked candidates, path-size metadata, selection, reroute, incident refresh and cache generations match the Python oracle for all declared backends and closures.

forbidden_changes: Do not change candidate ranking/tie breaks, route legality, cache keys or reroute thresholds.
Do not replace exact routing with a neural surrogate.

ordered_steps.action: Port graph-search and candidate data structures into the persistent Engine graph.
Replace per-call Vec inputs with references to engine-owned CSR and state arrays.
Port cache keys/generations and all invalidation triggers.
Port ranked K, path-size, stable tie breaks and reroute policy.
Shadow Python and Rust across no-route, incident, clear, loop, equal-cost and large-K fixtures.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_routing_engine_parity.py -k 'illegal or stale or no_route or equal_cost'

claim.allowed: Rust owns and reproduces routing and reroute semantics
claim.not_allowed: routing quality or CAPR benefit is established

stop_conditions: Route legality differs on any fixture.
Cache invalidation cannot be made exact.
Parallel graph search changes stable ordering.

pull_requests.title: Point/Spatial Queue, Turn, Signal, and Event-Effect Flow Port

objective.statement: Move the full flow authority, including discrete-agent token allocation and spatial queue, into Rust.
objective.observable_success: Rust matches link/node arrays, residual carries, sink/internal token allocation, storage receiving constraints, signals and incident effects tick by tick.

forbidden_changes: Do not retain the current restriction that spatial_queue_v1 must use Python.
Do not change token rounding, residual carry, queue capacity or signal timer semantics.
Do not enable fast-math.

ordered_steps.action: Port field arrays and point-queue continuous allocation.
Port discrete-agent service/receiving/sink token authority and residual carries.
Port spatial storage, spillback receiving constraints, signal timers and event multipliers.
Use checked segmented accumulations with deterministic order.
Run multi-tick parity, empty/zero-capacity, high-demand, spillback and simultaneous-turn fixtures.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_flow_event_parity.py -k 'zero_capacity or overflow or spillback or forbidden'

claim.allowed: Rust reproduces both declared traffic models and exact token authority
claim.not_allowed: the traffic model is empirically calibrated

stop_conditions: Mass closes only within a tolerance instead of exactly where tokens are integral.
spatial_queue_v1 remains Python-only.
Parallel accumulation changes results.

pull_requests.title: Active-Agent Allocation, Movement, Completion, and Failure Port

objective.statement: Move the full active-agent pool lifecycle and its queue transaction into Rust.
objective.observable_success: Allocation, movement, in-transit state, sink wait, completion/failure, cooldown and queue mutations match the Python oracle exactly.

forbidden_changes: Do not split agent and queue authority across languages.
Do not change slot allocation order, capacity behavior, completion transaction or failure codes.

ordered_steps.action: Port the pool to SoA with stable slot/trip IDs and checked capacity.
Port route ragged storage as offsets plus flat link IDs.
Port allocation, movement budgets, progress, sink wait, completion and typed failure.
Commit queue movement and agent movement in one Rust transaction.
Shadow pool arrays and ledgers after every tick on boundary fixtures.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_agent_engine_parity.py -k 'capacity or no_route or sink_wait or rollback'

claim.allowed: Rust owns the exact active-agent and queue transaction
claim.not_allowed: agent behavior is more realistic or optimal

stop_conditions: Python must mutate queues after Rust movement.
Slot order or completion codes differ.
Capacity overflow is silently dropped.

pull_requests.title: Land-Use, Accessibility, Policy Blend, and Learning-Memory Core Port

objective.statement: Move deterministic non-neural policy/runtime state and slow land-use/accessibility evolution into Rust while keeping model training orchestration optional in Python.
objective.observable_success: Enabled evolution cadence, accessibility values, blend bounds, bandit/plugin memory and baseline fallback semantics match the oracle; external learned models remain non-authoritative.

forbidden_changes: Do not make a neural model the route/state authority.
Do not train on external data.
Do not change causal lag or same-tick information rules.

ordered_steps.action: Port deterministic accessibility and land-use update rules with explicit cadence.
Port blend bounds, baseline fallback, bandit/plugin-memory updates and serialized state.
Define a narrow optional score-input interface for Python/JAX/Torch experiments without mutation authority.
Test causal delay, disabled-learning parity and malformed model output fallback.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_landuse_policy_parity.py -k 'same_tick or malformed or disabled or bounds'

claim.allowed: deterministic slow evolution and policy state have Rust parity
claim.not_allowed: learned policies are validated or authoritative

stop_conditions: A model output can mutate canonical state directly.
Same-tick feedback replaces the declared lag.
Disabled learning changes baseline output.

pull_requests.title: Complete Rust Tick Engine, Invariants, Replay, and Checkpoint

objective.statement: Compose all Rust domain ports into a single transactional Engine tick/chunk.
objective.observable_success: One Rust call executes the declared phase order, validates invariants, updates replay digest and supports checkpoint/restore with tick-by-tick Python shadow parity.

forbidden_changes: Do not change phase order to improve speed.
Do not validate only at the Python boundary.
Do not update state partially after an error.

ordered_steps.action: Implement Engine construction from accepted static and dynamic state.
Implement transactional phase sequencing and rollback-on-error.
Run invariants and digest inside Rust after each tick/chunk.
Implement checkpoint/restore including caches, RNG and cadence.
Shadow every tick across pause/events/closures/demand/spatial queue/learning-disabled scenarios.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_engine_tick_parity.py -k 'rollback or corrupt or checkpoint or phase_order'

claim.allowed: the complete Rust tick engine reproduces the frozen Python oracle scenarios

stop_conditions: Any phase still requires Python mutation.
Checkpoint omits a cache or RNG stream.
Error paths leave partial state.

pull_requests.title: Coarse PyO3 Engine API and NumPy Snapshot Boundary

objective.statement: Replace per-kernel Vec/list FFI with a thin persistent PyEngine object and coarse step/snapshot calls.
objective.observable_success: The Rust shadow path performs no `.tolist()`, no per-entity FFI and no Python state mutation; public snapshots and telemetry remain compatible.

forbidden_changes: Do not expose mutable NumPy aliases to canonical state.
Do not delete compatibility wrappers yet.
Do not turn snapshot export into a per-tick mandatory copy.

ordered_steps.action: Expose `PyEngine` create/apply/step/snapshot/checkpoint/restore/digest methods.
Release the GIL for step/chunk execution and convert Rust errors transactionally.
Use rust-numpy readonly arrays or explicit snapshot copies at observation boundaries.
Replace nested route vectors with offsets plus flat arrays.
Route old Rust kernel wrappers through compatibility code, not the default shadow engine.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_python_engine_api.py -k 'alias or missing_extension or panic or tolist'

claim.allowed: Python controls a persistent Rust engine through a coarse compatible API
claim.not_allowed: the Rust engine is default or zero-copy in every export

stop_conditions: A mutable snapshot can change engine state.
The shadow path still calls per-stage wrappers.
GIL release permits concurrent unsynchronized mutation.

pull_requests.title: Deterministic Rayon Parallelization and Thread-Budget Control

objective.statement: Parallelize independent engine work with an explicit engine-owned Rayon pool while preserving thread-count-independent results.
objective.observable_success: At 1/2/4/8 threads every canonical digest is identical, parallel work uses declared disjoint/fixed-combine patterns, and oversubscription is bounded.

forbidden_changes: Do not use unordered float reduce, float atomics, nondeterministic map iteration or the uncontrolled global Rayon pool.
Do not change algorithms solely to expose parallelism.

ordered_steps.action: Create an Engine-owned ThreadPool with explicit thread count and recorded policy.
Classify every parallel loop as disjoint write, indexed collect, integer reduction or fixed ordered float reduction.
Replace iteration-order-sensitive HashMap/HashSet outputs with sorted/indexed structures.
Test thread counts, repeated runs and nested-library thread budgets.
Measure scaling and overhead without changing correctness thresholds.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_parallel_simd_determinism.py -k 'unordered or oversubscription or thread_count'

claim.allowed: the Rust engine uses deterministic bounded CPU parallelism

stop_conditions: Any digest changes with thread count.
A canonical float result depends on Rayon reduction order.
Thread-pool interaction cannot be bounded.

pull_requests.title: SoA, Allocation, and Stable SIMD Optimization Pass

objective.statement: Optimize the complete Rust engine data path with contiguous SoA, allocation reuse, compiler vectorization and admitted stable SIMD only.
objective.observable_success: Criterion/perf evidence shows improved declared kernels without output drift, nightly Rust, fast-math or architecture-specific crashes.

forbidden_changes: Do not use nightly `std::simd` as the default.
Do not enable fast-math.
Do not accept microbenchmark wins that regress full engine wall time or memory.

ordered_steps.action: Remove avoidable per-tick allocation and reuse engine-owned buffers.
Align hot SoA loops for stable auto-vectorization and inspect generated code.
Add runtime-detected std::arch kernels only where copy-inclusive benchmarks justify them.
Keep a scalar implementation and exact parity tests for every manual SIMD kernel.
Measure complete engine, peak RSS and CPU feature fallback.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_parallel_simd_determinism.py -k 'scalar_fallback or unsupported_cpu or drift'

claim.allowed: the full Rust engine has evidence-backed stable CPU data-layout/SIMD optimizations
claim.not_allowed: nightly portable SIMD or every function is manually vectorized

stop_conditions: Only microbenchmarks improve while engine wall time regresses.
Manual SIMD changes a canonical result.
The implementation requires nightly Rust.

pull_requests.title: Optional Persistent GPU Kernel Admission

objective.statement: Evaluate and optionally admit one coarse device-resident numeric chunk without splitting canonical state authority.
objective.observable_success: A candidate is either admitted with copy/compile/drift/residency evidence or recorded HOLD; Rust CPU correctness/default progress is unaffected.

forbidden_changes: Do not move graph search, event control or branch-heavy agent authority to GPU by default.
Do not add eager GPU imports.
Do not hide host synchronization or compilation cost.
Do not admit a candidate solely on kernel-only speed.

ordered_steps.action: Freeze one or more tensor-shaped candidates from the complete Rust engine.
Try JAX primitives/Pallas before JAX FFI/custom CUDA; use PyTorch only for a real tensor/training need.
Design persistent device buffers and multi-tick chunking with explicit synchronization counters.
Measure compile, transfer, steady execution, VRAM, drift and failure behavior.
Admit, HOLD or reject each candidate without blocking Rust CPU promotion.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_gpu_admission.py -k 'eager or sync or drift or missing_gpu'

claim.allowed: the exact GPU candidates have an explicit ADMIT/HOLD/REJECT result
claim.not_allowed: GPU is required, faster globally, or scientifically validated

stop_conditions: GPU state requires per-tick host synchronization.
Drift exceeds preregistered field limits.
GPU absence changes Rust CPU behavior.

pull_requests.title: Full Shadow-Parity, Scale, Resource, and Performance Matrix

objective.statement: Run a preregistered Python-oracle versus Rust-engine matrix over all supported models, styles, scales, incidents, controls and thread counts.
objective.observable_success: All hard parity gates pass; complete performance/resource evidence meets promotion targets or the decision is HOLD without threshold changes.

forbidden_changes: Do not change engine code, oracle code, scenarios, tolerances or targets in this PR.
Do not drop failed, slow, no-route or OOM cases.
Do not report mean speed alone.

ordered_steps.action: Preregister the exact matrix and field-level parity rules before execution.
Run Python oracle and Rust at declared scales, traffic models, incidents and thread counts.
Record wall, Python wall share, FFI calls, peak RSS, allocations, replay digests and all failures.
Compute promotion result without averaging away a hard parity failure.
Preserve all negative results and issue PASS or HOLD.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_shadow_matrix.py -k 'missing_case or stale or threshold or failed_case'

claim.allowed: the exact frozen shadow matrix result and engineering speed/resource result
claim.not_allowed: global scientific validity or a guaranteed speedup on other workloads

stop_conditions: A matrix definition changes after results are seen.
Any hard parity case fails.
Performance targets are missed and someone proposes weakening them in the same PR.

pull_requests.title: Rust Default Backend and Python-Frontend-Only Cutover

objective.statement: Make the accepted Rust Engine the default runtime while retaining Python as frontend and an explicit oracle/debug backend.
objective.observable_success: Default configuration constructs PyEngine, stepping has one coarse Rust call per chunk, missing Rust fails closed, public APIs remain compatible, and Python oracle is explicit only.

forbidden_changes: Do not delete Python oracle tests.
Do not silently fall back.
Do not make GPU the default.
Do not change runtime default if RUST-PR-014 is HOLD.

ordered_steps.action: Require the exact PASS receipt from RUST-PR-014.
Replace fragmented edge/flow/routing/agent default selectors with one engine backend policy while maintaining compatibility parsing.
Route init/step/rollout/checkpoint/snapshot through PyEngine.
Keep `backend=python_oracle` explicit for debug/tests and fail closed if Rust is unavailable.
Update docs and run all public API/CLI/UI/benchmark regressions.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_default_backend.py -k 'missing or silent or gpu or hold'

claim.allowed: the supported default runtime is Rust-owned with a Python frontend
claim.not_allowed: Python is removed, GPU is default, or empirical traffic validity is established

stop_conditions: RUST-PR-014 does not have a PASS receipt.
Any default path silently executes Python.
Public frontend behavior cannot be preserved.

pull_requests.title: Fresh-Context Final Audit, Cleanup, and Migration Decision

objective.statement: Independently audit the complete migration, remove only proven-dead compatibility surfaces, and freeze the bounded final decision.
objective.observable_success: A fresh reviewer reports P0=0/P1=0, every evidence fingerprint is current, no default-path per-kernel bridge remains, and the final APPROVE/HOLD/REJECT package is reproducible.

forbidden_changes: Do not modify scientific algorithms, performance targets or benchmark definitions.
Do not delete compatibility code still used by the oracle or public API.
Reviewer must not fix code in first pass.

ordered_steps.action: Start a fresh-context audit-only reviewer with base/final SHA, actual diff, contracts and raw logs.
Return P0/P1/P2/P3 findings with file:line, violated invariant and reproducer.
Send P0/P1 back to the implementer; repeat review after fixes.
Remove only compatibility wrappers proven unused by static and dynamic tests.
Build a final decision package that cites exact receipts and stops assurance expansion.

negative: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rust_engine_final_audit.py -k 'stale or same_reviewer or missing or p0 or p1'

claim.allowed: the exact final migration decision and bounded supported architecture
claim.not_allowed: future workloads are guaranteed faster or the research model is scientifically validated

stop_conditions: Fresh reviewer is not independent.
Any evidence receipt is stale or missing.
Cleanup would delete an oracle/publicly used path.
